dicto-alice.name: Alice
dicto-alice.note: W49: cell-first, in a gap (cut at its midpoint), 144 corners; a gap section, not in Boole Stott's series; not found in the sources checked (#63)

dicto-alicia.name: Alicia
dicto-alicia.note: W48: the cell-first central slice of the 600-cell, the middle section of Alicia Boole Stott (1900, cell-first series through the corner layers); named after her by DICTO

dicto-bandersnatch.name: Bandersnatch
dicto-bandersnatch.note: W60: cell-first corner-layer section, one of the sections of Alicia Boole Stott (1900, cell-first series through the corner layers)

dicto-blockhead.name: Blockhead
dicto-blockhead.note: not found in the sources checked (#56): the twinned octet's tetrahedral-hole piece at 3/8, the twin of the cube

dicto-chucky.name: Chucky
dicto-chucky.note: not found in the sources checked (#57): a Janus c/h piece of ABAC at -3/8 (hexagonal top half, cubic bottom half); its volume is the mean of its two parents'

dicto-cube-pearl.name: Cube Pearl
dicto-cube-pearl.note: the cube with its edges cut back by the planes (±1, ±1, 0)·x ≤ 6/5 (depth s = 3/5): 32 corners all on one sphere, 6 squares and 12 hexagons, Oh; the chamfered-cube family is classical, this depth was not found in the sources checked; its chain of T closes with period four (#80)

dicto-david.name: David
dicto-david.note: known shape: a tetragonal disphenoid, the empty Cr4 tetrahedron of A15 moved by half a body diagonal (#55 Corollary 1); the name is DICTO's

dicto-delilah.name: Delilah
dicto-delilah.note: known shape (regular octahedron), of edge 2^(-1/3) at octet edge 1; DICTO's name for it at the Delian bond (#51)

dicto-dodecaxes.name: Dodecaxes
dicto-dodecaxes.note: not found; the Unborn Axes with 8 Tricap keys, holding a whole regular dodecahedron (#48 Theorem 3)

dicto-fang.name: Fang
dicto-fang.note: not found in the sources checked (#57): a Janus c/h piece of ABAC at 5/24 (hexagonal top half, cubic bottom half); its volume is the mean of its two parents'

dicto-ganesha.name: Ganesha
dicto-ganesha.note: not found in the sources checked (#61): the Janus c/h tetrahedral piece of a squashed stacking (cubic bottom, hexagonal top); in the dataset at the parameters of #61 Figure 1 (ACBC, layer spacing^2 = (3/4)(2/3), lambda = 1/10)

dicto-golden-clasp.name: Golden Clasp
dicto-golden-clasp.note: the faces of the truncated cuboctahedron at depths 1 : 1/φ : 3/4 on the 4-, 3- and 2-fold axes (48 corners, 26 faces, Oh); its chain of T closes with period four, while the Archimedean truncated cuboctahedron's does not (Star Cores study 3)

dicto-golden-ti-star.name: Golden TI Star
dicto-golden-ti-star.note: the truncated icosahedron with a pyramid on every face, tips at φ × the feet of the perpendiculars (92 corners, 180 triangles, volume φ × TI, Ih); the doubling form (2×) is the same construction; not found in the sources checked (#78)

dicto-goliath.name: Goliath
dicto-goliath.note: known shape: the classical Z12 coordination icosahedron of A15 (Frank and Kasper 1958), the convex hull of Jessen's orthogonal icosahedron (Jessen 1967) scaled by 1/2; here the A15 power cell at weight difference 3/4 (#55: the tiling is the classical picture of A15 shifted by half a body diagonal); the name is DICTO's

dicto-gti.name: DICTO GTI (golden truncated icosahedron)
dicto-gti.note: cycle and pieces not found; Bergman US 4,719,726 has octet-like shells

dicto-haigha.name: Haigha
dicto-haigha.note: R33: 120-cell edge-first slice, the only one with nine-sided faces; not found in the sources checked (#65)

dicto-hamlet.name: Hamlet
dicto-hamlet.note: step 5 of the chain of DICTO's growth rule T from the Ogdoecontahedron, after KRE, PHE, TPP and DPHP: 452 corners, 270 faces, Ih (#80, Section 6)

dicto-hatta.name: Hatta
dicto-hatta.note: R35: 120-cell edge-first slice, the other 114-corner slice; not found in the sources checked (#65)

dicto-hecatodihedron.name: DICTO Truncated-Icosahedral Hecatodihedron (DICTO Hecatodihedron, TIH)
dicto-hecatodihedron.note: derived from a known solid (jtI with 12 five-fold corners cut flat; #28 V2); not found named

dicto-humpty-dumpty.name: Humpty Dumpty
dicto-humpty-dumpty.note: known (corrected in version 5): the cell-first section of the 600-cell at height 1 + sqrt5/2, one of the sections drawn by Alicia Boole Stott (1900, cell-first series through the corner layers), read for #63 version 3; the exact solid, the convex egg of 92 triangles (Td) and the name are #63's and DICTO's; D85 is kept (D-numbers are never reused); its forced equal-edged form is Fallen Humpty (#63; Slice-48 in #62, numeric only, not in the dataset)

dicto-ian-dury.name: Ian Dury
dicto-ian-dury.note: not found in the sources checked (#56): the twinned octet's tetrahedral-hole piece at the stop 5/24, beside the classical 60 deg rhombohedron

dicto-icosaxes-hexa.name: Icosaxes Hexa
dicto-icosaxes-hexa.note: eight Icosaxes round an Unborn Axes as one solid (= nine Icosaxes passing through each other), the node of the Icosaxes Kagome network; the network was not found in the sources searched (#59)

dicto-icosaxes.name: Icosaxes
dicto-icosaxes.note: known shape: Koca et al. 2015 non-regular truncated octahedron x = tau (semi-uniform truncated octahedron); new route (the golden split of the AXE in the icosahedron lattice, #48); the name is DICTO's

dicto-jabberwock.name: Jabberwock
dicto-jabberwock.note: W3: vertex-first, the largest all-triangle slice of the 600-cell (72 corners, 140 triangles); not found as a solid in the sources checked (#63)

dicto-jewel.name: DICTO Jewel (EKP windows; first called Dragon Jewel)

dicto-jubjub.name: Jubjub
dicto-jubjub.note: W43: face-first all-triangle slice (30 corners, 56 triangles); not found as a solid in the sources checked (#63)

dicto-keyaxes.name: Keyaxes
dicto-keyaxes.note: the piece of the keyed Icosaxes Kagome network (the Icosaxes with 2 Tricap dents and 6 mirrored Tricap keys, volume phi^2); the network was not found in the sources searched (#59)

dicto-kre.name: DICTO KRE (Kite-Rhombic Enneacontahedron)
dicto-kre.note: combinatorics of the rhombic enneacontahedron (known type); this metric solid new

dicto-lahdeli.name: Lahdeli
dicto-lahdeli.note: not found in the sources checked (#56): the twinned octet's octahedral-hole piece at its equal-volume point, Delilah's twin

dicto-lion.name: Lion
dicto-lion.note: W1: the vertex-first central slice of the 600-cell (42 corners, 80 triangles, Ih); not found as a solid in the sources checked (#63)

dicto-lotus-hexa.name: Lotus Hexa
dicto-lotus-hexa.note: the keyed Icosaxes Hexa: eight corner pieces dented towards a Dodecaxes and keyed outward (mirrored Tricaps) on their other seven hexagons (#59)

dicto-lotus-jewel-axes.name: Lotus Jewel Axes
dicto-lotus-jewel-axes.note: not found; the Icosaxes with 8 Tricap dents (#48 Theorem 3)

dicto-mad-hatter.name: Mad Hatter
dicto-mad-hatter.note: W28: face-first, in a gap (cut at its midpoint), one of the four 144-corner slices, all different; not found in the sources checked (#63)

dicto-march-hare.name: March Hare
dicto-march-hare.note: W30: face-first, in a gap (cut at its midpoint), 144 corners; not found in the sources checked (#63)

dicto-metaxyhexecontahedron.name: DICTO Metaxyhexecontahedron
dicto-metaxyhexecontahedron.note: new as a named, distinguished member; the dodecahedron-icosahedron hull family is known

dicto-ogdoecontahedron.name: DICTO Ogdoecontahedron (OG)
dicto-ogdoecontahedron.note: face arrangement known (dual of L0(D), Antiprism); derived from the canonical pentakis dodecahedron (#31 V2)

dicto-ophelia.name: Ophelia
dicto-ophelia.note: step 6 of the same chain, after Hamlet: 642 corners, 440 faces, Ih (#80, Section 6); the chain does not close

dicto-palintriacontahedron.name: DICTO Palintriacontahedron
dicto-palintriacontahedron.note: new as a named, distinguished member; the dodecahedron-icosahedron hull family is known

dicto-phe.name: DICTO PHE (Pentagon-Hexagon Enneacontadihedron)
dicto-phe.note: face counts of Goldberg GP(3,0); this solid new

dicto-red-king.name: Red King
dicto-red-king.note: R77: 120-cell pentagon-first central slice, two regular decagons; the polar of the 600-cell's edge-first shadow; not found in the sources checked (#65)

dicto-red-knight.name: Red Knight
dicto-red-knight.note: R113: 120-cell cell-first slice in a gap (cut at its midpoint), 120 corners; a gap section, not in Boole Stott's series; not found in the sources checked (#65)

dicto-samson.name: Samson
dicto-samson.note: new proportion: the cube with four alternate corners cut, at the Delian bond; not found in the sources (#51)

dicto-shadow-17.name: Kagemusha
dicto-shadow-17.note: DICTO's name 2026-10-30, the shadow warrior (was Shadow-17, a placeholder from the 2D view; file slug dicto-shadow-17 kept); new construction from a known piece (J11, Johnson's gyroelongated pentagonal pyramid, Johnson 1966): two J11 glued on their pentagons; #62 identifies it as the equal-edged form of the 600-cell's outer edge-first slices; status decided by DICTO 2026-10-28; placeholder name of #62

dicto-skewed-ed-16.name: DICTO skewed elongated dodecahedron (ED F16)
dicto-skewed-ed-16.note: new member of a known family (ED parallelohedra: Fedorov; Lalvani US 5,623,790)

dicto-skewed-ed-18.name: DICTO skewed elongated dodecahedron (ED F18)
dicto-skewed-ed-18.note: new member of a known family (ED parallelohedra: Fedorov; Lalvani US 5,623,790)

dicto-skewed-rhombic-dodecahedron.name: DICTO skewed rhombic dodecahedron
dicto-skewed-rhombic-dodecahedron.note: new member of a known family (RD parallelohedra: Fedorov 1885; Lalvani US 5,623,790, 1997)

dicto-sonsam.name: Sonsam
dicto-sonsam.note: not found in the sources checked (#56): the twinned octet's tetrahedral-hole piece at its equal-volume point (19 corners, a nine-sided face on the mirror plane); #56: easy to compute, so an unnamed drawing may exist

dicto-star-halo.name: Star Halo
dicto-star-halo.note: DICTO's name: the hull of the TI Star's 32 tips, a pentakis dodecahedron that is not the Catalan one (five-fold corners 1.0265 × further out than the six-fold ones); not found in the sources checked (#78)

dicto-ti-star-core.name: TI Star core
dicto-ti-star-core.note: the icosahedron truncated at 1/φ³ of each edge (12 pentagons, 20 hexagons, hexagon edges in the ratio √5), the core of every turn of the TI Star cycles and the polar partner of the Star Halo (#78)

dicto-triskelion-tetrahedron.name: Triskelion Tetrahedron
dicto-triskelion-tetrahedron.note: the cubic octet's tetrahedral piece at 5/24, a member of Samson's sliding family (#51); met in ABAC and named in #57 (the name marks that member)

dicto-tweedledee.name: Tweedledee
dicto-tweedledee.note: W22: edge-first slice (32 corners, 60 triangles, D5h), another shape with Tweedledum's counts; not found as a solid in the sources checked (#63)

dicto-tweedledum.name: Tweedledum
dicto-tweedledum.note: W5: vertex-first slice (32 corners, 60 triangles, Ih); not found as a solid in the sources checked (#63)

dicto-unborn-axes.name: Unborn Axes
dicto-unborn-axes.note: known shape: Koca et al. 2015 non-regular truncated octahedron x = 1/tau; new route (#48); the name is DICTO's

dicto-unicorn.name: Unicorn
dicto-unicorn.note: W58: cell-first corner-layer section, one of the sections of Alicia Boole Stott (1900, cell-first series through the corner layers); same counts as the Lion, another shape

dicto-walrus.name: Walrus
dicto-walrus.note: R80: 120-cell pentagon-first slice, 120 corners; not found in the sources checked (#65)

dicto-white-knight.name: White Knight
dicto-white-knight.note: R115: 120-cell cell-first slice in a gap (cut at its midpoint): the faces and symmetry of the truncated icosidodecahedron (30 squares, 20 hexagons, 12 decagons, Ih) with two edge lengths; not found in the sources checked (#65)

dicto-white-rabbit.name: White Rabbit
dicto-white-rabbit.note: W51: cell-first, in a gap (cut at its midpoint), 144 corners; not found in the sources checked (#63)
